page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at top, page number at top right. Heading and subtitle at the head of the column. Short marginal reference signs stand at the left edge of several lines, inside the text block. Catchword at the foot right, signature at the foot left.

main_text.head: Exercitatio. XLII.
De peccato Davidis numerantis populum. 2.Sam.24.
main_text.p: A' ποεία[?] : videtur David non peccasse.
Ratio: quia fecit ex lege Exod.30. & ex officio.

p.i: Principis est virtus maxima nosse suos.

main_text.p: Antithesis sit propositio: Sed graviter peccavit.
Ratio 1. quia multa gravia peccata in eo facto concurrunt.
1. Superbia & elatio animi, ut possit gloriari de multitudine.
Amplif. comparatione cum peccato Hiskiae, ostentantis thesauros 1.Reg.24. Et Nebucadnezaris exclamantis: Haec est illa Babylon.
2. Confidentia propriae potentiae, qua contra hostes, se tutum putavit magis quam Dei praesidio.
3. Curiositas, quod nulla urgente necessitate census instituit.
4. Avaritia, quia simul censu novo, ut fit probabile, fiscum regium explere voluit.
Ergo non ex officio: quia Principis virtus est nosse suos non ad ostentandum, vel deglubendum, sed ad tuendum & benefaciendum.
Ratio 11. Quia contra legem census instituit.
Ostendatur, quod lex census populi non permisit nisi justa de causa, & cum pensione semisicli in fiscum tabernaculi.

page.notes: The Greek words at the start of the first and second-last lines are printed in a light italic Greek hand; the reading of the first ("ἀπορία", set as printed "ποεία") is uncertain and marked. The catchword "Ratio" and the signature "Q j." stand at the foot. Show-through from the facing page and the neighbouring page edge at the left are not transcribed. Small marks before "Antithesis" and "Amplif." are section signs and are not printed text.
